subject.title: [Feature Request] Telegram Channel: Support Thread Binding for Subagent Sessions

question: Should Telegram expose explicit child-topic native subagent session spawning now, and should that be done through the current core session-binding adapter path while keeping default top-level Telegram placement as current?
rationale: Current main has the adapter primitives, but the remaining behavior affects Telegram topic creation, model-visible capability exposure, plugin/API shape, and default visibility of child work, which requires maintainer intent before implementation or closure.

options.title: Review or replace the active Telegram PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82023 as the main design input, resolve ownership and visibility findings, rebase it, and require final-head live Telegram proof before merge.

options.title: Defer child-topic spawning
options.body: Keep Telegram current-conversation binding as the only supported default and leave this issue open until maintainers decide the visibility and API model for child topics.

options.title: Reject Telegram child-topic subagent spawning
options.body: Close this issue and associated candidate PRs as not planned if maintainers decide internal subagent work should never create Telegram topics.

recommendation.title: Review or replace the active Telegram PR
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82023 as the main design input, resolve ownership and visibility findings, rebase it, and require final-head live Telegram proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The core adapter path and current policy/tool gates trace most strongly to this recent thread-binding work.
